Q: RuntimeError: There is no current event loop in thread in async + apscheduler A:

I had a similar issue where I wanted my asyncio module to be callable from a non-asyncio script (which was running under gevent... don't ask...). The code below resolved my issue because it tries to get the current event loop, but will create one if there isn't one in the current thread.

Tested in python 3.9.11.

try:
    loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
except RuntimeError as e:
    if str(e).startswith('There is no current event loop in thread'):
        loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
        asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)
    else:
        raise

Q: "Use Strict" needed in a TypeScript file? A:

In the context of Node.js being able to execute typescript files directly by stripping the type information since version 22.18.0 (see https://nodejs.org/api/typescript.html) it might not be obvious that it could become relevant (again) to add 'use strict'; to your typescript files under certain circumstances:

You can test this in your project by adding the file isStrict.ts

console.log({isStrict: (() => !this)()});

and executing it using node ./isStrict.ts

See https://stackoverflow.com/a/10480227/684134 for an explanation of the script.

If Nodejs considers your file being a CommonJS file it will log {isStrict:false} !

Here are the reasons why Nodejs might run the script in strict mode:

  • you have configured "type": "module" in your package.json file

  • you added es module syntax like import ... or export default ... to the file (nodejs detects is and triggers a warning)

  • the file has an extension of .mjs

  • you added 'use strict'; (or "use strict";) to the beginning of the file

For more detailed information check https://nodejs.org/api/typescript.html#determining-module-system

So if you still need to run (typescript) CommonJS files, and you want them to run in strict mode, you need to add 'use strict'; to the top of the file. Otherwise just stick to ES modules, which is the better option nowadays.

PS: When I run the same script using Bun, it works the same way. Running it in Deno executes it in strict mode, most likely because Deno transpiles instead of just stripping the types.

Q: Exception in C# code when trying to call a stored procedure with encrypted param A:

Try to use: Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 5.x+

Important: remove ForceColumnEncryption = false.

As I understand that your param is encrypted and column value also encrypted.

Q: Chrome network tools override content not working A:

This is a known bug/issue. It's easier to bypass if you have control of the server you can disabling the cache buster parameters by removing ?_= parameter. If not you could try breaking on the request and manually modify the response in the sources panel although this isn't ideal
